questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: If the double mass curve analysis of rainfall data for a station shows a sudden change in slope, the most probable cause(s) is/are:
questions.questionText: If the double mass curve analysis of rainfall data for a station shows a sudden change in slope, the most probable cause(s) is/are:

options.html: Shifting of rainfall station to a new position.
options.text: Shifting of rainfall station to a new position.

options.html: Increase or decrease in rainfall intensity.
options.text: Increase or decrease in rainfall intensity.

options.html: Change in the vicinity of the station due to growth of trees.
options.text: Change in the vicinity of the station due to growth of trees.

options.html: Rain gauge may be faulty from a certain period.
options.text: Rain gauge may be faulty from a certain period.

questions.explanationHtml:
(a, c, d)
The causes of inconsistency of rainfall records/sudden change in slope of double mass curve
are:
(i) Shifting of rainfall station to a new location.
(ii) When ecosystem in the vicinity is changed due to land slide, forest fire, flood and earthquake.
(iii) Error in observation from a certain year.
(iv) Change in the vicinity of the station due to growth of trees, building, fencing, cutting of
forest nearby changing the wind pattern, etc.
(v) Rainguage may be faulty from a certain period.
(vi) Site of instrument may be changed or replaced without record.

questions.questionText: Correctly match the shape of catchment (List I) to the shape of hydrograph obtained for that catchment (List II) and select the correct code:
questions.explanationHtml:
(a)
• Shape of the catchment influences the time taken by a water particle in reaching the outlet from the farthest point of the catchment and hence it influences the time after which peak discharge is obtained.
• Fan shaped i.e. nearly semicircular shaped catchments give high peak and narrow hydrographs
while elongated catchments give low-peaked and broad hydrographs.

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: In the moving boat method used for streamflow measurement, which of the following parameters must be measured to accurately determine discharge?
questions.questionText: In the moving boat method used for streamflow measurement, which of the following parameters must be measured to accurately determine discharge?

options.html: Velocity measured by the current meter, water depth and speed of the boat.
options.text: Velocity measured by the current meter, water depth and speed of the boat.

options.html: Velocity and direction of the current meter, water depth and time interval between depth measurements.
options.text: Velocity and direction of the current meter, water depth and time interval between depth measurements.

options.html: Water depth, time interval between measurements, boat speed and stream velocity.
options.text: Water depth, time interval between measurements, boat speed and stream velocity.

options.html: Velocity and direction of the current meter along with the speed of the boat.
options.text: Velocity and direction of the current meter along with the speed of the boat.

questions.explanationHtml:
(b)
In the moving boat method, discharge is calculated by integrating the flow across the stream
cross-section while the boat moves from one bank to the other. The essential parameters include:
1. Velocity and direction of flow
2. Water depth
3. Time interval between successive measurements
• In practice, it is the water velocity vector (relative to boat and earth) that is measured, not
boat speed itself.
